senses.gloss:
vyutthānasaṁskāra
(‘impressions of the waking state’)
------------------------------------------
According to the Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) the मिन्द् generally has two states: vyutthāna (rising) and nirodha (suppressed). The rising of the vṛttis (mental waves) is prompted by the सṁस्कारस् (past impressions) lurking in the मिन्द्.
The science of योग advises the aspirant to suppress the rising of the vṛttis by using the steps recommended by it. This is technically called nirodha, the same as cittavṛttinirodha (Yogasūtras 1.2). As nirodha or suppression is practised more and more, the nirodhasaṁskāra (impression in the मिन्द् that helps in the suppression of the vṛttis) becomes stronger. Once this is achieved the मिन्द् becomes more and more quiet and peaceful (vide Yogasūtras 3.9, 10).
